questions.question: Fruits and seeds have a high concentration of which of the following plant hormones?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Cytokinin**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Cytokinins are a group of plant hormones that promote cell division and growth in plant roots and shoots.
 
• They are known to delay the aging of plant tissues by inhibiting protein degradation and promoting protein synthesis and mobilization of nutrients.
 
• Cytokinins are synthesized in the roots and transported to other parts of the plant, including fruits and seeds, where they are present in high concentrations.
 
• In fruits and seeds, cytokinins play a crucial role in cell differentiation and development, as well as in the delay of senescence.
 
• They work synergistically with other hormones like auxins to regulate various growth processes and morphogenesis in plants.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Auxin**

 
 
• Auxins are another group of plant hormones that primarily regulate cell elongation, especially in the stem and root tips.
 
• They are involved in various growth processes including phototropism, gravitropism, and the formation of lateral and adventitious roots.
 
 
 
• **Gibberellin**
 
 
• Gibberellins are plant hormones that promote stem elongation, seed germination, and flowering.
 
 
• **Abscisic Acid (ABA)**
 
 
• Abscisic acid is a plant hormone that primarily functions in stress responses, such as closing stomata during water stress.
 
• It also plays a role in seed dormancy and inhibition of growth, helping plants to survive adverse conditions.

questions.question: Variegated leaves are found in which of the following plants?

• Neem is valued for its medicinal properties.

questions.question:
Justify the given statement:

‘Plants have low energy needs’.

options.text: Plant bodies have a small proportion of dead cells in many tissues.
As the plants use relatively fast transport systems.
Because plants are autotropic organisms and prepare their own food.
Energy needs differ between different body designs. Plants do not move and have a large proportion of dead cells in many tissues.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Energy needs differ between different body designs. Plants do not move and have a large proportion of dead cells in many tissues.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Plants have a large proportion of dead cells in many tissues, which do not require energy.
 
• Unlike animals, plants do not move from one place to another, reducing their energy needs.
 
• Energy needs differ between different body designs; the stationary nature of plants results in lower energy requirements.
 
• Dead cells in plants provide structural support without the need for energy.
 
• Plants primarily rely on sunlight for energy through photosynthesis, which is a relatively low-energy process compared to the metabolic activities of animals.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Plant Transport Systems**

 
 
• Plants have specialized transport systems like xylem and phloem to move water, nutrients, and food.
 
• Xylem transports water and minerals from roots to other parts of the plant.
 
• Phloem distributes the food prepared by leaves to different parts of the plant.
 
 
 
• **Photosynthesis**
 
 
• Plants use sunlight to convert carbon dioxide and water into glucose and oxygen.
 
• This process occurs in the chloroplasts of plant cells and is essential for the survival of plants.
 
 
 
• **Autotrophic Organisms**
 
 
• Plants are autotrophic, meaning they can produce their own food through photosynthesis.
 
• This reduces their dependency on other organisms for energy.

questions.question: Which is the internal energy reserve in plants?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Starch**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Starch is a **polysaccharide** that serves as a form of energy storage in plants.
 
• It is composed of numerous **glucose units** joined together by glycosidic bonds.
 
• Plants synthesize starch during photosynthesis and store it generally in plastids.
 
• Starch can be broken down into glucose molecules when the plant needs energy for growth and other metabolic activities.
 
• It is a **complex carbohydrate** that is insoluble in water, making it a good storage form of energy.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Glycogen**

 
 
• It is a polysaccharide of glucose that serves as a form of energy storage in animals and fungi.
 
• Glycogen is stored primarily in the liver and muscle cells.
 
 
 
• **Glucose**
 
 
• It is a simple sugar and a primary source of energy for cells.
 
• Glucose is involved in cellular respiration to produce ATP.
 
 
 
• **Sucrose**
 
 
• It is a disaccharide composed of glucose and fructose.
 
• Sucrose is commonly found in plants and is used for energy transport.

questions.question: What is the function of xylem?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Conduction of water and minerals**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The primary function of xylem is the **conduction of water and minerals** from the roots to the rest of the plant.
 
• Xylem is made up of various types of cells, including tracheids and vessel elements, which are specialized for water transport.
 
• The structure of xylem allows it to support the plant mechanically while conducting water.
 
• Xylem tissues are typically found in vascular plants, forming a continuous network from the roots to the leaves.
 
• In addition to water and mineral transport, xylem also plays a role in storing nutrients and providing structural support to the plant.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Phloem**

 
 
• Phloem is responsible for transporting organic nutrients, particularly sucrose, from the leaves to other parts of the plant.
 
• It consists of different cell types, including sieve tube elements and companion cells.
 
 
 
• **Root Hairs**
 
 
• Root hairs are extensions of root epidermal cells that increase the surface area for water and mineral absorption.
 
• They play a crucial role in anchoring the plant and facilitating nutrient uptake from the soil.
 
 
 
• **Transpiration**
 
 
• Transpiration is the process by which water evaporates from the aerial parts of the plant, primarily through stomata in the leaves.
 
• This process helps in the upward movement of water through the xylem and also in cooling the plant.

questions.question: Which elements of xylem tissue form interconnected water-conducting channels?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Vessels and Tracheids**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Xylem is a type of vascular tissue in plants responsible for the conduction of water and nutrients from the roots to the rest of the plant.
 
• Vessels and tracheids are the primary water-conducting elements in the xylem tissue.
 
• Vessels are long tubes formed by the end-to-end connection of vessel elements, allowing efficient water transport.
 
• Tracheids are elongated cells with tapered ends that overlap each other, facilitating water movement through their pits.
 
• Both vessels and tracheids have thick, lignified walls that provide structural support to the plant.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/8bcced9228da63df94044622ceab189bf61874ec72cd8b35477d549969e0e950.png] 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Xylem Fibers**

 
 
• These are supportive fibers present in the xylem that provide mechanical strength to the plant.
 
• They are not involved in water conduction.
 
 
 
• **Phloem**
 
 
• It is another type of vascular tissue responsible for the transport of nutrients, particularly sugars, from the leaves to other parts of the plant.
 
• Phloem consists of sieve tube elements, companion cells, phloem fibers, and phloem parenchyma.
 
 
 
• **Plant Roots**
 
 
• Roots absorb water and minerals from the soil and transport them to the xylem.
 
• They also anchor the plant and store nutrients.

questions.question: Cells of the meristematic tissue are very active, but they lack:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**vacuoles**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Meristematic tissue cells are highly active and are involved in continuous cell division.
 
• These cells possess a dense cytoplasm which supports their high metabolic activity.
 
• The cells have thin cellulose walls that provide flexibility and support for cell division.
 
• Meristematic cells contain prominent nuclei which are essential for regulating cell division and growth.
 
• These cells generally lack vacuoles or have very small vacuoles because vacuoles are more prominent in mature cells and are involved in storage and maintenance of cell turgor.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Parenchyma Cells**

 
 
• These are the most common type of plant cells and are found in various parts of the plant.
 
• They have thin cell walls and large central vacuoles.
 
• Parenchyma cells are involved in storage, photosynthesis, and tissue repair.
 
 
 
• **Collenchyma Cells**
 
 
• These cells provide structural support to growing parts of the plant.
 
• They have thicker cell walls compared to parenchyma cells and are typically found in stems and leaves.
 
 
 
• **Sclerenchyma Cells**
 
 
• These cells are known for their thick, lignified cell walls which provide mechanical support.
 
• Sclerenchyma cells are found in non-growing regions of the plant such as the bark and mature stems.

questions.question: The _____ moves water and minerals obtained from the soil while ______ transports products of photosynthesis from the leaves where they are synthesised to other parts of the plant.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**xylem, phloem**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Xylem** is responsible for the transport of water and minerals from the roots to other parts of the plant.
 
• **Phloem** is responsible for the transport of the products of photosynthesis, primarily sugars, from the leaves to other parts of the plant.
 
• Xylem consists of vessels and tracheids, which are tubular structures that facilitate the upward movement of water and minerals.
 
• Phloem consists of sieve tubes and companion cells, which work together to transport nutrients throughout the plant.
 
• The process of water transport in xylem is largely driven by transpiration and root pressure, whereas phloem transport is driven by the pressure-flow mechanism.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Collenchyma**

 
 
• It is a type of plant tissue that provides support and flexibility to growing parts of the plant such as stems and leaves.
 
• Collenchyma cells have thicker cell walls compared to parenchyma cells and are often found under the epidermis.
 
 
 
• **Parenchyma**
 
 
• It is the most common type of plant tissue, involved in various functions including photosynthesis, storage, and tissue repair.
 
• Parenchyma cells have thin cell walls and large vacuoles, making them versatile in function.
 
 
 
• **Sclerenchyma**
 
 
• It is a type of plant tissue that provides structural support due to its thick, lignified cell walls.
 
• Sclerenchyma cells are usually dead at maturity and include fibers and sclereids.

questions.question: What is the position of the apical meristematic tissue in a plant body?

options.text: At the growing tips of the stems and roots
Near to the root region only
On the lateral side of the stem and roots

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**At the growing tips of the stems and roots**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The apical meristematic tissue is located at the **growing tips of the stems and roots** of a plant.
 
• It is responsible for the **primary growth** of the plant, which results in an increase in length.
 
• These tissues contain **actively dividing cells** that contribute to the elongation of the plant.
 
• The apical meristem is crucial for the formation of new organs such as leaves, flowers, and roots.
 
• It plays a significant role in the **development and growth** of the plant, ensuring continuous growth at the tips.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Lateral Meristems**

 
 
• These are found on the lateral sides of stems and roots.
 
• Lateral meristems are responsible for the secondary growth, which increases the girth of the plant.
 
 
 
• **Intercalary Meristems**
 
 
• These are located at the base of leaves or internodes.
 
• They help in the regrowth of grasses and elongation of internodes.
 
 
 
• **Root Cap**
 
 
• A protective structure that covers the tip of a root.
 
• It protects the apical meristem as the root pushes through the soil.

questions.question: Which of the following is the most common simple permanent tissue?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Parenchyma**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Parenchyma is the most common simple permanent tissue found in plants.
 
• It consists of living cells that are thin-walled, and is usually involved in storage, photosynthesis, and secretion.
 
• These cells are generally isodiametric in shape, meaning they have roughly equal dimensions on all sides.
 
• Parenchyma cells have large central vacuoles that store nutrients and waste products.
 
• They also play a role in the healing and repair of plant tissues due to their ability to divide and differentiate.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Epidermis**

 
 
• The epidermis is the outermost layer of cells in plants, serving as a protective barrier against environmental factors.
 
• It helps in reducing water loss and provides protection against pathogens.
 
 
 
• **Phloem**
 
 
• Phloem is a complex tissue responsible for the transport of nutrients, particularly sugars produced by photosynthesis, in plants.
 
• It consists of various cell types, including sieve elements, companion cells, phloem fibres, and parenchyma.
 
 
 
• **Sclerenchyma**
 
 
• Sclerenchyma is a type of permanent tissue known for its role in providing mechanical support and strength to plant structures.
 
• It consists of dead cells with thick, lignified cell walls.

questions.question:
Select the correct sentence(s).

a. The release of energy in the aerobic process is a lot greater than in the anaerobic process.

b. ATP is broken down giving rise to a fixed amount of energy which can drive the endothermic reactions taking place in the cell.

c. The pyruvate is converted into lactic acid which is also a three-carbon molecule.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**option 3**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The release of energy in the aerobic process is significantly greater than in the anaerobic process.
 
• ATP (Adenosine Triphosphate) is broken down to release a fixed amount of energy which can drive the endothermic reactions taking place in the cell.
 
• Pyruvate, a three-carbon molecule, is converted into lactic acid, which is also a three-carbon molecule during anaerobic respiration.
 
• In aerobic respiration, glucose is fully oxidized to carbon dioxide and water, producing a high yield of ATP.
 
• Anaerobic respiration is less efficient and results in the production of less ATP and byproducts like lactic acid or ethanol.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Cellular Respiration**

 
 
• This is a set of metabolic reactions and processes that take place in the cells of organisms to convert biochemical energy from nutrients into ATP.
 
• It involves both aerobic and anaerobic pathways depending on the presence of oxygen.
 
 
 
• **Glycolysis**
 
 
• It is the first step in both aerobic and anaerobic respiration, taking place in the cytoplasm of the cell.
 
• Glycolysis breaks down glucose into two molecules of pyruvate, yielding a net gain of two ATP molecules.
 
 
 
• **Fermentation**
 
 
• It is an anaerobic process by which cells generate energy through the conversion of glucose to lactic acid or ethanol.
 
• Fermentation allows cells to produce ATP without oxygen, though it is much less efficient compared to aerobic respiration.

questions.question: Yeast is commonly used in kitchen for baking and brewing. The scientific name for baker's yeast is _______.

• In baking, the carbon dioxide produced during fermentation causes the dough to **rise and become fluffy**.
 
• In brewing, it is used to ferment sugars into **alcohol** and carbon dioxide, essential for producing beer and other alcoholic beverages.
 
• **Saccharomyces cerevisiae** is also extensively used as a model organism in **genetic and molecular biology research** because of its simple genome and ease of cultivation.
 
• It has been used by humans for thousands of years, making it one of the earliest domesticated microorganisms.

• This bacterium helps in the **fermentation of lactose** into lactic acid.

 __

questions.question: Plastids are vital organelles in plant cells. Which of the following is a function of plastids?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Photosynthesis**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Plastids are organelles unique to plant cells and algae, responsible for key functions such as **photosynthesis**, storage, and synthesis of compounds.
 
• **Chloroplasts**, a type of plastid, contain chlorophyll pigments that absorb light energy and convert it into chemical energy during photosynthesis.
 
• Photosynthesis occurs in the **thylakoid membranes** of chloroplasts, where sunlight is used to synthesize glucose from carbon dioxide and water.
 
• Plastids also contribute to the synthesis of essential molecules such as **amino acids** and **lipids**, which are critical for plant metabolism.
 
• In addition to photosynthesis, plastids like amyloplasts store starch, and chromoplasts contribute to pigment production, offering versatility to plant functions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Plastids:**

 
 
• Plastids are **double-membraned organelles** found in plants and algae, classified into chloroplasts, chromoplasts, and leucoplasts based on their functions.
 
• They play an essential role in processes such as **photosynthesis**, **storage**, and **pigment synthesis**.
 
 
 
• **Chlorophyll:**
 
 
• Chlorophyll is a green pigment found in chloroplasts, critical for capturing light energy for photosynthesis.
 
• It absorbs light most efficiently in the **blue and red wavelengths** while reflecting green light.
 
 
 
• **Photosynthesis Equation:**
 
 
• The chemical equation for photosynthesis is: **6CO₂ + 6H₂O + Light → C₆H₁₂O₆ + 6O₂**.
 
• It occurs in two stages: **Light-dependent reactions** and **Calvin Cycle**.
 
 
 
• **Other Plastid Types:**
 
 
• **Chromoplasts:** Responsible for synthesizing and storing pigments that give fruits and flowers their vibrant colors.
 
• **Leucoplasts:** Non-pigmented plastids involved in the storage of starch, oils, or proteins.

questions.question: The transport of water and minerals primarily occurs through which part of a plant?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Xylem**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Xylem** is the vascular tissue in plants responsible for transporting water and dissolved minerals from the roots to other parts of the plant.
 
• It primarily consists of specialized cells such as **tracheids** and **vessels**, which facilitate the movement of water through capillary action and adhesion-cohesion forces.
 
• **Xylem transport** is a unidirectional process, moving water and nutrients upward from the roots to the leaves.
 
• The process of water movement in xylem is driven by **transpiration pull**, which occurs due to water evaporation from stomata in the leaves.
 
• Xylem also provides structural support to plants, as its cells develop thick, lignified walls.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Phloem:** Unlike xylem, phloem transports organic compounds like sugars and amino acids, primarily from leaves to other parts of the plant (bidirectional transport).

questions.question: Mendel studied traits such as flower colour and seed shape in pea plants. These traits are called as:

• These visible characters are observable features that can be seen in the phenotype of the organisms.
 
• The traits Mendel studied include seven different characters: flower color, flower position, seed color, seed shape, pod shape, pod color, and plant height.
 
• These traits follow Mendelian inheritance patterns, where dominant and recessive alleles determine the visible characters.

• Genetic codes are sequences of nucleotides in DNA or RNA that determine the amino acid sequence of proteins.
 
• They are not directly observed as traits but are crucial in the process of trait expression.
 
 
 
• **Dominant Characteristics:**
 
 
• Dominant characteristics are traits that are expressed in the phenotype even when only one copy of the allele is present.
 
• For example, in Mendel's experiments, the yellow seed color is a dominant characteristic.
 
 
 
• **Progeny Units:**
 
 
• Progeny units refer to the offspring resulting from a cross or breeding experiment.
 
• They are not traits but the next generation that inherits the traits.
 
 
 
• **Mendelian Inheritance:**
 
 
• It refers to the patterns of inheritance first described by Gregor Mendel in the 19th century.
 
• Key principles include the laws of segregation and independent assortment.
 
 
 
• **Phenotype:**
 
 
• The phenotype is the set of observable characteristics of an individual resulting from the interaction of its genotype with the environment.
 
• Visible characters are part of the phenotype.

questions.question: By which of the following processes, do plants release water from the structures called 'hydathodes', on the edges or margins of leaves?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Guttation**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Guttation is the process of loss of plant sap in the form of droplets from the leaf margins or tips.
 
• It occurs when two of the following conditions are present:
 
 
• transpiration is low due to low evaporation rate.
 
• water absorption is high due to high root pressure.
 
 
 
• Thus, guttation is not observed in tall trees where the force required for guttation will be too high.
 
• It is usually observed in grasses and mustard plant.
 
• Guttation takes place through special structures on the leaves called hydathodes.
 
• Hydathodes are small pores at the tips and margins of the leaf, which are used to remove the surplus xylem sap of the plants.
 
• The pores of hydathodes remain open at all times.
 
• The droplets that are exuded contain dissolved substances along with water.
 
• Guttation is usually observed at midnight or early morning.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Wilting**:

 
 
• Wilting is a visible symptom of water stress in plants.
 
• It occurs when the plant loses more water than it can absorb from the soil, leading to a loss of turgor pressure in plant cells.
 
• This causes leaves and stems to droop and become limp.
 
• Severe wilting can permanently damage or even kill the plant.
 
• Wilting can be caused by various factors, including drought, excessive heat, and soil compaction.
 
 
 
• **Cytomixis**:
 
 
• Cytomixis is a rare phenomenon observed in plant cells, particularly during meiosis.
 
• It involves the migration of chromatin material (DNA) from one cell to another through cytoplasmic connections.
 
• This abnormal exchange of genetic material can lead to chromosomal abnormalities in the resulting offspring.
 
• The exact causes of cytomixis are not fully understood, but it is believed to be influenced by environmental factors and genetic predisposition.
 
 
 
• **Cavitation**:
 
 
• Cavitation is the formation of air bubbles within the xylem vessels of plants.
 
• It occurs when the water column within the xylem is disrupted, leading to the formation of air embolisms.
 
• These air bubbles block the flow of water and nutrients from the roots to the leaves, causing significant stress to the plant.
 
• Cavitation can be triggered by various factors, including drought, high temperatures, and freezing.

questions.question: Which of the following plant components is/are tasked with conveying water and nutrients from the roots to other parts of the plant?

questions.question: In the process of photosynthesis, what happens to the carbohydrates (glucose) that are produced?

• This storage process ensures that plants have a steady supply of energy to maintain their metabolic activities.

• This ability to regulate water content is crucial for **plant survival**, especially in varying environmental conditions.
 
• The vacuole, a large central organelle in plant cells, plays a key role in storing and regulating water within the cell.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Carbon Dioxide**__

 __
 
• **Carbon dioxide (CO2)** is a gas that plants use during the process of **photosynthesis** to produce glucose and oxygen.
 
• It is not involved in changing the shape of plant cells by swelling or shrinking.
 
 
 
• **Fat**__
 __
 
• **Fat** is a type of lipid and is primarily used by plants for **energy storage**.
 
• It does not play a role in the process of changing the shape of plant cells.
 
 
 
• **Chlorophyll**__
 
 
• **Chlorophyll** is a green pigment found in the chloroplasts of plant cells.
 
• It is essential for **photosynthesis** as it helps absorb light energy, but does not contribute to cell shape alteration.

questions.question: The roots of a plant always grow downwards while the shoots usually grow upwards and away from the earth. This upward and downward growth of shoots and roots is known as:
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**geotropism**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Geotropism** is the growth of plant roots downward, towards the earth, and the growth of shoots upward, away from the earth.
 
• This type of movement is also known as **gravitropism**, as it is influenced by gravity.
 
• **Roots** exhibit positive geotropism as they grow downward into the soil.
 
• **Shoots** exhibit negative geotropism as they grow upward away from the earth.
 
• This growth orientation helps the plant to anchor itself and access water and nutrients from the soil.
 
• Geotropism ensures that the plant's leaves are exposed to sunlight for photosynthesis.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Hydrotropism**__

 __
 
• **Hydrotropism** is the growth movement of a plant in response to water.
 
• Roots exhibit positive hydrotropism as they grow towards moisture.
 
• This response helps plants to find and absorb water from the soil.
 
 
 
• **Chemotropism**__
 __
 
• **Chemotropism** is the growth of plants in response to a chemical stimulus.
 
• An example is the growth of pollen tubes towards the ovules, guided by chemicals released by the ovules.
 
• This is crucial for the process of fertilization in flowering plants.
 
 
 
• **Phototropic Movement**__
 
 
• **Phototropic movement** is the growth of a plant in response to light.
 
• Shoots generally exhibit positive phototropism by growing towards the light source.
 
• This helps the plant to maximize light absorption for photosynthesis.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is correct about transport in plants?

options.text: The phloem moves water and minerals obtained from the soil.
In herbs and shrubs, the distances over which transport systems have to operate are very large.
The xylem transports products of photosynthesis from the leaves where they are synthesised to other parts of the plant.
Plants have low energy needs and use relatively slow transport systems.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Plants have low energy needs and use relatively slow transport systems.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Plants, being autotrophic organisms, produce their own food via photosynthesis, which significantly reduces their overall energy needs compared to animals.
 
• The transport of water, minerals, and nutrients in plants occurs through xylem and phloem, which are relatively slow compared to the circulatory systems in animals.
 
• Plants rely on processes such as diffusion, osmosis, and active transport to move substances, which do not require high energy expenditure.
 
• Due to the stationary nature of plants and their low metabolic rates, the slow transport system suffices to meet their needs.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Xylem**

 
 
• Xylem is responsible for the transport of water and dissolved minerals from the roots to other parts of the plant.
 
• It consists of vessels and tracheids, which are long, tube-like structures that facilitate the movement of water.
 
• The process of water movement in xylem is driven by transpiration pull, root pressure, and capillary action.
 
 
 
• **Phloem**
 
 
• Phloem is responsible for the transport of organic nutrients, particularly sucrose, from the leaves to other parts of the plant.
 
• It consists of sieve tubes, companion cells, phloem fibers, and phloem parenchyma.
 
• The movement in phloem is bidirectional, allowing nutrients to be transported to growing regions and storage tissues.
 
 
 
• **Transpiration**
 
 
• Transpiration is the process by which water vapor is lost from the aerial parts of plants, primarily through stomata.
 
• This process creates a negative pressure in the leaf, which helps in pulling water up through the xylem from the roots.
 
 
 
• **Photosynthesis**
 
 
• Photosynthesis is the process by which green plants use sunlight to synthesize nutrients from carbon dioxide and water.
 
• It primarily occurs in the chloroplasts of plant cells and produces glucose and oxygen as by-products.
 
• The products of photosynthesis are transported through the phloem to various parts of the plant for growth and storage.
